title: The Hollow Garden
premise: Elodie Voss survives in the valley of Hollowmere by stealing memories from travelers and selling them to the memory-brokers, since magic cannot cross the valley's borders and neither can she. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue, Elodie discovers the girl carries the last living seed of the Verdant Court — the magic that once kept the long winter at bay — and that the brokers intend to harvest it, reigniting the ancient war between the Court and the Frostbound. Fleeing the valley for the first time, Elodie must learn to give memories back instead of taking them, discovering her own stolen childhood among them. In the end she plants the seed in the frozen heart of the old court at the cost of her own collected past, choosing an unwritten future over a hoarded one as spring finally breaks the winter.
about_author: Edmund Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from mountain villages before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about inheritance, memory, and the quiet violence of surviving at someone else's expense.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She lifts a soldier's memory of his mother's kitchen and sells it to broker Maren Hale, then returns to her hovel above the frost line. The beat establishes her transactional loneliness: she owns hundreds of lives but has none of her own.

chapters.title: A Knock Before the Snow
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A child appears at her door during the first snowfall, mute, speaking a language no one in the valley knows. Elodie recognizes the words from a stolen memory of a dying king. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Brokers Pay For
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren inspects the child and realizes what she carries, sending word to the Frostbound sympathizers beyond the valley. Beat: cold ambition; the reader sees the trap closing while Elodie remains blind.

chapters.title: The Valley That Magic Forgot
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She tests the child near the border stones and watches a flower bloom through ice, confirming magic lives in the girl. Terror and wonder war in her; for the first time she considers leaving Hollowmere.

chapters.title: Thieves' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Brokers come for the child; Elodie trades away her most valuable stolen memory to buy a night's head start. Beat: the first real sacrifice, and the discovery that giving hurts differently than stealing.

chapters.title: Over the Stones
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with the child (Wren) beginning to communicate through shared memories Elodie lends her. They cross the border into a world where magic hums visibly. Beat: vertigo and awe; Elodie's senses flood with returned sensation.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered through impressionistic memory-language. Wren shows Elodie fragments of the Verdant Court's fall. Beat: the child becomes a person, not cargo; Elodie feels belonging stir uncomfortably.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Inn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They shelter with a retired Frostbound deserter, Tam, who explains the coming long winter and the war it ended. Beat: exposition delivered as grief; Tam warns that both sides will use Wren.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Hedgerow
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Broker hunters arrive; Tam holds them off and dies buying the pair time. Beat: the cost of kindness made literal; Elodie inherits Tam's map and guilt.

chapters.title: The City of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach Vellum, where memories are currency and Elodie's thefts are known. An old mark recognizes her face from a stolen life. Beat: shame externalized; she must hide inside identities she stole.

chapters.title: A Debt in Someone Else's Name
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. To move freely, Elodie begins returning stolen memories to their original owners, one by one, each return weakening her but buying passage. Beat: restitution as penance; she finds her own childhood memory in a broker's vault.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Elodie
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She recovers her own earliest memory: her mother was a Verdant Court gardener who hid her in the valley. Beat: devastating revelation — she is herself an heir of the Court, and Wren was sent to find her.

chapters.title: Winter's Ambassadors
chapters.summary: Frostbound envoy Corvane's POV. Corvane offers Elodie a bargain: hand over Wren and receive her mother, held in stasis since the war. Beat: temptation sharpened into cruelty; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: What Mothers Would Ask
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie nearly accepts, meeting her frozen mother briefly. Wren's silent plea breaks the moment. Beat: the lowest point; Elodie chooses betrayal, then un-chooses it at the door.

chapters.title: Flight Through the White Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Pursued by brokers and Frostbound alike, they flee across the frozen wilds toward the ruined Court. Wren falls ill as the seed strains against the cold. Beat: desperation; Elodie gives Wren warm memories to keep her alive.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne of Green
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach the dead court, a garden turned to glass. Elodie learns the planting requires a keeper's whole remembered life. Beat: dread crystallizing into acceptance; she understands the true price.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Gate
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Frostbound arrive offering mercy one final time; Maren Hale, revealed as Corvane's agent, urges Elodie to take the deal. Beat: every debt called in at once; betrayal and loyalty collide.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The final blizzard descends; Wren is dying, the seed dimming. Elodie begins feeding the seed her memories — the kitchens, the thefts, her mother's face. Beat: climax begins as willing loss.

chapters.title: Everything I Stole, Given Back
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She empties herself completely, returning even the memory of why she came. The garden ignites green beneath the snow; Corvane's host falters before living things. Beat: climax — annihilation of self transfigured into spring.

chapters.title: Spring, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes in a blooming court, tended by a woman who doesn't know her name but stays anyway. Beat: tender aftermath; love persisting without memory.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Daughter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, fragmentary. With returned scraps from those she once robbed, Elodie rebuilds a modest self. She chooses to remain as the court's new gardener. Beat: identity as something grown, not inherited or stolen.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Next Winter
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Years later, Wren and Elodie teach valley children the old tongue and send seeds outward. The long winter is broken but not defeated. Beat: resolution — inheritance redefined as stewardship, and belonging chosen rather than bought.
